recognize_zh: 周邊血液抹片中箭頭所指為循環母細胞：核大、染色質細緻、細胞質少且偏藍，旁邊還有帶空泡的單核球與分葉核嗜中性球；在急性骨髓性白血病的背景下代表母細胞進入周邊血。
features: Circulating blasts (arrows) with high N:C ratio, round nucleus and fine chromatin
Scant to moderate basophilic, agranular cytoplasm
Monocytes with folded nuclei and cytoplasmic vacuoles
Segmented and band neutrophils with normal-appearing granulation
Red cells mostly normocytic with mild anisocytosis; platelets appear decreased in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows circulating blasts (arrows) with a high N:C ratio, round nuclei with fine chromatin and scant basophilic cytoplasm. There are admixed segmented neutrophils, bands and monocytes, some of which contain cytoplasmic vacuoles. Red cells show mild anisocytosis without significant poikilocytosis, and platelets appear reduced in this field. No Auer rods are identified. Findings are consistent with circulating blasts in the setting of acute myeloid leukemia.

ddx.vs: Reactive lymphocytes have more abundant cytoplasm that hugs adjacent red cells and condensed chromatin, not the fine blast chromatin seen here.
These show a left shift with myelocytes and metamyelocytes and nucleated red cells, with only rare blasts.
Lymphoblasts can look identical on smear; flow cytometry (TdT, CD19/CD3 vs MPO/CD13/CD33) is required.
Lymphoma cells often have nuclear clefts or clumped chromatin and express mature B- or T-cell markers without CD34.
